listing.shortDescription: Admission aggregate from board and test marks with custom or verified weights.

title: Merit & Aggregate Calculator (Custom Weights)
description: Calculate your admission merit aggregate from Matric, Intermediate, entry test and interview marks, with custom weights or verified NUST and MDCAT presets.
quickAnswer: Aggregate = Σ (marks obtained ÷ total marks × weight %). With Matric 900/1100 at 10%, Intermediate 950/1100 at 40% and an entry test 300/400 at 50%, the aggregate is 8.18 + 34.55 + 37.50 = 80.23%. The weights must add up to 100%, and every university sets its own, so confirm them in the official prospectus for your admission year.

formula.title: Merit Aggregate Formula
formula.explanation: Each component (Matric/SSC, Intermediate/HSSC, entry test, interview and so on) is first turned into a percentage of its own total, so a test out of 200 and a board exam out of 1100 can be compared. That percentage is multiplied by the component's weight, and the weighted parts are added. Because the weights total 100%, the result is itself a percentage from 0 to 100. The calculator keeps full precision until the end and rounds the aggregate to 2 decimal places.

variables.name: Obtained / Total
variables.description: Your marks in that component and the maximum possible, exactly as on your result card.

variables.name: Weight
variables.description: The share of the aggregate the institution gives that component, in %. All weights together must equal 100%.

variables.name: Contribution
variables.description: Your percentage in the component × its weight ÷ 100: the points it adds to your aggregate.

commonMistakes.title: Using last year's weights
commonMistakes.description: Universities and regulators change their merit formulas, sometimes every year. Always check the weights in the official prospectus or admission notice for the session you are applying to.

commonMistakes.title: Adding raw marks instead of percentages
commonMistakes.description: Adding 900 board marks to 150 test marks gives a number that means nothing, because the totals differ. Each component must be turned into a percentage of its own total before it is weighted.

commonMistakes.title: Entering the wrong total
commonMistakes.description: Board totals differ between Matric schemes and boards, and some formulas use HSSC Part-1 marks only. Copy the total exactly from your result card and from the institution's rules.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting hafiz-e-Quran or other additions
commonMistakes.description: Some institutions add extra marks or deduct marks for repeated attempts. These rules vary, so add them yourself according to the official prospectus.

commonMistakes.title: Rounding each component
commonMistakes.description: Rounding every contribution before adding can move the final aggregate by a few hundredths, which matters on close merit lists. The calculator keeps full precision and rounds only the final result.

howto.name: How to Calculate a Merit Aggregate
howto.description: Combine board results, entry tests and interviews into an admission aggregate.

steps.name: Choose custom or a preset
steps.text: Use Custom to type any weights, or pick a verified preset to fill in its components and weights.

steps.name: Enter your marks
steps.text: For each component, type marks obtained and total marks exactly as on your result card.

steps.name: Check the weights
steps.text: Make sure the weights add up to 100% and match the official prospectus for your admission year.

steps.name: Read your aggregate
steps.text: See each component's percentage and contribution, and your aggregate to two decimal places.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my merit aggregate?
faqs.a: Divide your marks by the total marks for each component, multiply by that component's weight, and add the results. For 900/1100 at 10%, 950/1100 at 40% and 300/400 at 50% the aggregate is 80.23%.

faqs.q: What is the NUST aggregate formula?
faqs.a: For admission on NET basis, NUST's published criteria are NET 75%, HSSC (Part-1 or full) 15% and SSC/O Level 10%. Choose the NUST preset, enter your marks, and check NUST's merit criteria page for the current session.

faqs.q: What is the MDCAT aggregate formula?
faqs.a: Under the PM&DC Admissions, Curriculum and Conduct Regulations 2026, open merit admission to public and private medical and dental colleges uses MDCAT 50%, FSc/HSSC 40% and SSC/Matric 10%. Your admitting university publishes the final criteria.

faqs.q: Why does the calculator say my weights must total 100%?
faqs.a: An aggregate is a weighted percentage, so the weights must cover the whole 100%. If they add up to 90%, a component or part of a weight is missing; check the institution's formula.

faqs.q: Can I add an interview or a second test?
faqs.a: Yes. Custom mode accepts up to five components. Give each a name, marks obtained, total marks and weight.

faqs.q: Where are the weights for UET ECAT or other universities?
faqs.a: This calculator only includes presets that were checked against an official source. For any other university, use Custom mode and copy the weights from its current prospectus.

faqs.q: Is my calculated aggregate the official one?
faqs.a: No. It is an estimate from the marks and weights you enter. The admitting institution's own calculation and merit list are final.

always-check-the-official-prospectus.heading: Always Check the Official Prospectus
always-check-the-official-prospectus.p1: Merit formulas are set by each university, medical regulator or admitting authority, and they change. Weights shift between Matric, Intermediate and entry tests; some institutions use HSSC Part-1 marks only, add an interview, or treat O/A Level equivalence differently. Before you rely on any aggregate, open the official prospectus or admission notice for your session and compare its formula with the weights you entered.
always-check-the-official-prospectus.p2: This calculator includes presets only where the weights were checked against an official source, and each preset shows that source and the date it was checked:
always-check-the-official-prospectus.p3: For any other university, choose Custom and copy the weights from its prospectus. If the formula includes something this calculator does not, such as extra marks for hafiz-e-Quran or a deduction for an improvement attempt, apply that adjustment to your marks first.

improving-your-aggregate.heading: Improving Your Aggregate
improving-your-aggregate.li1: Look at the weights: a component with a 50% or 75% weight moves your aggregate far more than one at 10%. Under NUST's formula, each extra NET percentage point adds 0.75 to your aggregate.
improving-your-aggregate.li2: Know what is fixed: your Matric marks are usually final by the time you apply; your entry test and sometimes your Intermediate marks are not.
improving-your-aggregate.li3: Compare with past merit: institutions often publish closing merit from previous years. Treat them as a rough guide only; they change with the number of applicants and seats.
